record.original_question: For the Riesz s-energy with radial external field V(x)=γ‖x‖^α/α, what is the structure of the equilibrium measure μ_eq in the regime max{−s,0} < α < α_{s,d}, where α_{s,d} is the sharp threshold above which the equilibrium support is a sphere? For example, can the minimizer split into several components such as multiple spheres together with isolated points?

evidence.quote: Question 1.3 (Robert Womersley, Edward Saff). What can we say about the equilibrium measure for values of α with max{−s, 0} < α < αs,d?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Fix integers $d\ge 2$ and a parameter $s$ with $-2<s<d$ (with $s\ne 0$; the value $s=0$ corresponds to the logarithmic kernel). For $x,y\in\mathbb{R}^d$ define the Riesz $s$-kernel
$$k_s(x,y)=\begin{cases}\|x-y\|^{-s},&s\ne 0,\\ -\log\|x-y\|,&s=0,\end{cases}$$
and, for parameters $\gamma>0$ and $\alpha>\max\{-s,0\}$, define the radial external field
$$V(x)=\frac{\gamma}{\alpha}\,\|x\|^{\alpha},\qquad x\in\mathbb{R}^d.$$
For a Borel probability measure $\mu$ on $\mathbb{R}^d$ consider the weighted Riesz energy
$$\mathcal{E}_{s,V}(\mu)=\iint k_s(x,y)\,d\mu(x)\,d\mu(y)+2\int V(x)\,d\mu(x).$$
Under the stated assumptions there exists a unique compactly supported probability measure $\mu_{\mathrm{eq}}=\mu_{\mathrm{eq}}(s,d,\alpha,\gamma)$ minimizing $\mathcal{E}_{s,V}$ over all Borel probability measures of finite energy.

It is known that there is a sharp threshold $\alpha_{s,d}>\max\{-s,0\}$ such that for every $\alpha\ge \alpha_{s,d}$ the support of $\mu_{\mathrm{eq}}$ is a sphere centered at the origin (with explicit uniform density on that sphere), while for $\alpha<\alpha_{s,d}$ this is not the case.

Determine the structure of $\mu_{\mathrm{eq}}$ in the sub-threshold regime
$$\max\{-s,0\}<\alpha<\alpha_{s,d}.$$
In particular, characterize the support of $\mu_{\mathrm{eq}}$: can it consist of several disjoint components, e.g.\ a union of finitely many concentric spheres, possibly together with isolated points or lower-dimensional pieces, and in each case give the corresponding density of $\mu_{\mathrm{eq}}$.
artifact.status_search_result: The sharp threshold $\alpha_{s,d}$ above which the equilibrium support is a sphere was characterized in work by Chafaï, Matzke, Saff and collaborators ("Riesz Energy with a Radial External Field: When is the Equilibrium Support a Sphere?", Potential Analysis 63 (2025), 705–738; arXiv:2405.00120). The structure of the equilibrium measure in the sub-threshold regime $\max\{-s,0\}<\alpha<\alpha_{s,d}$ is explicitly posed there as an open question (attributed to Womersley and Saff), and we found no publication resolving it.

status_evidence.title: Riesz Energy with a Radial External Field: When is the Equilibrium Support a Sphere?
status_evidence.snippet: Characterizes the values of the power for which dimension reduction occurs (the support of the equilibrium measure becomes a sphere); the sub-threshold regime is left open.
status_evidence.claim: Establishes existence of the threshold but does not describe the equilibrium measure for $\alpha<\alpha_{s,d}$.

status_evidence.title: Radial Riesz equilibrium on a sphere – Djalil Chafaï
status_evidence.snippet: Discussion of the threshold for the radial Riesz equilibrium on a sphere; sub-threshold structure flagged as not yet understood.
status_evidence.claim: Author's blog post indicates the sub-threshold structure of the equilibrium measure remains unresolved.
